chapters.title: Chapter 4: Valuing Stocks Across the Cycle

body.text: Never value a cyclical on the earnings it made this year. Value it on what it would earn in an ordinary year, at an ordinary margin, on the business as it stands today. That single change turns the P/E from a trap into a usable tool.

markDefs.definition: An estimate of what a company would earn in a typical year of its business cycle, removing the effect of unusually good or bad years.

children.text: The last lesson ended with a fix for the cyclical P/E paradox: change the denominator. This lesson builds that denominator properly.

are the profits a company would make in a typical year, neither boom nor bust. There are three common ways to estimate them, each with a clear weakness, and the most practical one for Indian investors can be done in minutes with Screener.in data.

cells: Average the last 8 to 12 years of EPS
Ignores growth: a company twice as big today is valued on its smaller past
Apply the average operating margin across a cycle to today's revenue
Reflects today's scale while removing margin extremes
Today's revenue may itself be inflated or depressed by prices
Multiply the average return on equity across a cycle by today's book value
Works well for banks and capital-heavy businesses
Book value can be distorted by write-offs, impairments, and acquisitions

children.text: The Mid-Cycle Margin Method, Step by Step

markDefs.definition: The operating profit margin a cyclical company earns in a typical year, usually estimated as the average or median margin across at least one full cycle.

children.text: The idea is to keep today's scale but replace today's margin with a typical one. Operating margin is the line that swings most across a cycle, as the Tata Steel case showed, so it is the line you normalise. Depreciation and interest change slowly and are largely fixed, so you take them at current levels. The

body.caption: OPM = operating profit margin, as shown in Screener.in's Profit and Loss table
Illustrative CementCo: peak year vs normalised, ₹ crore

children.text: A margin that is 8 percentage points above normal inflates EPS by 80%, from ₹30 to ₹54. On peak EPS, CementCo looks cheap at 10 times. On normalised EPS, the same price is 18 times, which may be perfectly reasonable for a quality cement maker, or expensive, depending on its peers and growth. Either way, you are now comparing like with like.

body.title: Calculate Normalised EPS
body.prompt: An aluminium company has revenue of ₹8,000 crore. Its mid-cycle operating margin is 15%. Depreciation is ₹300 crore, interest is ₹100 crore, the tax rate is 25%, and it has 20 crore shares. What is its normalised EPS in rupees?
body.explanation: Operating profit = 8,000 × 15% = ₹1,200 crore. Profit before tax = 1,200 - 300 - 100 = ₹800 crore. Net profit = 800 × 75% = ₹600 crore. Normalised EPS = 600 ÷ 20 = ₹30.

children.text: Now the real thing. Tata Steel's consolidated operating margin from FY15 to FY26 ranged from -0.6% to 26%. Its 12-year average was 13.1%. FY26's margin was 15%, above that average.

stats.label: Trailing P/E on reported FY26 EPS of ₹8.65
P/E on mid-cycle margin EPS of ₹6.06

children.text: Two useful checks come out of this. First, the model is calibrated: plugging in FY26's actual 15% margin gives EPS of ₹8.48, close to the reported ₹8.65, so the simplifying assumptions are reasonable. Second, both normalisation methods tell the same story. With FY26 margins above the 12-year average, the trailing P/E of about 22 flatters the valuation. On typical margins, the stock is priced at a little over 30 times normalised earnings. That is not a verdict on whether to buy. It is a far more honest starting point than the headline P/E.

body.text: Historical averages assume the future cycle will look like the past one. For Tata Steel, that is debatable. The 12-year window includes years of heavy European losses, and the UK business has since been restructured towards electric arc furnaces while Indian capacity has grown. If the business mix has genuinely improved, the true mid-cycle margin going forward may be higher than 13.1%. If competition from Chinese exports intensifies, it may be lower. Normalisation replaces one number you cannot trust with an assumption you must defend.

body.title: Why not just average past EPS?

children.text: Averaging EPS is quick, and for Tata Steel it happens to land close to the margin method: ₹5.75 against ₹6.06. But the method has a built-in bias for any company that has grown. Tata Steel's revenue was ₹1,39,504 crore in FY15 and ₹2,32,140 crore in FY26. Averaging EPS gives equal weight to years when the business was far smaller. For a company that has doubled its capacity, average EPS will understate what it can earn today, making it look more expensive than it is.

The margin method fixes the scale problem but introduces a subtler one: today's revenue may be inflated by high commodity prices. Professional analysts go one step further and normalise revenue too, multiplying current sales volume by a mid-cycle realisation per tonne. For most individual investors, the margin method with a sensitivity range is a good balance of accuracy and effort.

body.caption: Judgement calls and how to make them

cells: At least one full cycle, peak to peak or trough to trough; for metals and cement, usually 8 to 12 years
Calculate both. The median is less affected by one extreme boom or bust year
Exclude years distorted by accounting changes or exceptional events, and say so
Adjust for major acquisitions, demergers, closures, or capacity shifts that change the margin structure
Never use a single number. Show a range, such as median, average, and a conservative case

body.title: Pick the Better Denominator
body.question: A steel company has doubled its capacity over the last eight years. Its current operating margin is at a 10-year high. Which normalised earnings estimate is most appropriate?
options: The average EPS of the last eight years
This year's EPS, because it reflects the larger capacity
Current revenue multiplied by the median operating margin across the last full cycle, less current depreciation and interest, after tax
The lowest EPS of the last eight years, to be conservative
body.explanation: Average EPS understates earning power because the company is now much bigger. This year's EPS is inflated by a peak margin. The lowest EPS reflects a smaller business in its worst year. Applying a median cycle margin to current scale removes the margin extreme while keeping today's size. You would still sense-check whether current revenue is inflated by high steel prices.

body.title: Two Analysts, Two Answers
body.scenario: Two analysts value the same cement company. Analyst A uses the 10-year average operating margin of 17% and gets a normalised P/E of 22. Analyst B argues the industry has consolidated sharply, with the top few players now controlling most capacity, so she uses the 5-year average margin of 20% and gets a normalised P/E of 17. A mutual fund investor reading both reports is confused about which to trust.
body.prompt: How should the investor think about the difference between the two analysts?
body.modelAnswer: Neither analyst is making a calculation error; they disagree about what 'normal' looks like going forward. Analyst A assumes the future cycle will resemble the past decade. Analyst B assumes consolidation has permanently improved pricing power, so older, lower-margin years are less relevant. The investor should test Analyst B's claim: has industry concentration actually increased, have margins held up in recent weak demand periods, and is significant new capacity coming that could undo the discipline? If consolidation is real and durable, B's higher mid-cycle margin is justified. If new capacity is arriving, A's more conservative view is safer. The practical approach is to treat 17 to 22 times as a range and to ask which assumption the current share price already reflects.

body.title: Normalise Any Cyclical in 20 Minutes
steps: From Screener.in's Profit and Loss table, copy 10 to 12 years of OPM %, plus the latest year's Sales, Depreciation, Interest, and Tax %
Calculate the average and median OPM, and note the highest and lowest years
Compute normalised net profit at the median margin, the average margin, and a conservative margin
Divide by the current share count (latest net profit ÷ latest EPS gives a close approximation)
Check calibration: plug in the latest actual margin and confirm your EPS is close to reported EPS
Calculate P/E on each normalised EPS at today's share price
Write down whether the business has changed enough to justify a different mid-cycle margin, and why

points: Normalised earnings estimate what a cyclical would earn in a typical year, replacing unreliable current EPS
Average EPS is simple but understates earning power for companies that have grown
The mid-cycle margin method applies a typical operating margin to today's revenue, then deducts current depreciation, interest, and tax
For Tata Steel, above-average FY26 margins meant a trailing P/E near 22 versus about 31 on mid-cycle margins
Always calibrate the model against reported EPS and show a range of margins rather than a single answer
Adjust the mid-cycle margin only when the business or industry structure has genuinely changed, and be explicit about why

body.text: Tata Steel figures are consolidated annual data as displayed on Screener.in at the time of writing and a closing price of ₹188.75 on 9 September 2026 from historical market data. The normalised calculations use simplifying assumptions: a 32% tax rate, share count derived from reported net profit and EPS, and no adjustment for other income or minority interests. CementCo, the aluminium example, and the analysts' scenario are illustrative. This lesson is educational and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
